screening_decisions.reason: This is a review article about FIGO staging classification for endometrial cancer, not a randomized controlled trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. It discusses surgical-pathological staging rather than treatment comparisons.

This is an RCT comparing doxorubicin alone versus doxorubicin plus cyclophosphamide in 356 patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma no longer amenable to surgery, radiotherapy, or progestins. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.

This is a Phase III RCT comparing two chemotherapy regimens (doxorubicin+cisplatin vs doxorubicin+paclitaxel+filgrastim) in chemotherapy-naïve patients with endometrial cancer. Meets selection criteria as it compares different chemotherapy regimens in advanced disease.
This is a methodological paper about standardization of reporting results of cancer treatment, not a clinical trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a retrospective review of pelvic exenteration (surgical procedure) for recurrent endometrial cancer, not a randomized controlled trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is an RCT comparing adriamycin versus cyclophosphamide in patients with advanced endometrial cancer with measurable disease no longer amenable to standard surgical or radiotherapeutic treatment. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.

This is a randomized phase II trial comparing cisplatin alone versus CAP combination in 30 progestin-refractory patients with metastatic endometrial carcinoma. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.

This is a randomized phase II trial comparing cyclophosphamide versus ifosfamide in 61 patients with recurrent or metastatic endometrial adenocarcinoma. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.
This is an overview of randomized trials about beta blockade for myocardial infarction, not related to endometrial cancer or chemotherapy. Completely irrelevant to the review question.

This is an RCT comparing two chemotherapy regimens (melphalan+5-FU+megace vs adriamycin+5-FU+cyclophosphamide+megace) in 358 patients with advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.
This is a methodological paper about extracting statistics for meta-analysis, not a clinical trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a Phase III RCT comparing MVAC versus AC chemotherapy regimens in patients with advanced endometrial cancer. Although terminated early due to slow accrual, it meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.

This is a Phase III RCT comparing doxorubicin+cisplatin versus doxorubicin+cisplatin+paclitaxel+filgrastim in 273 women with advanced or recurrent endometrial carcinoma. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.
This trial is about chemotherapy for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), not endometrial cancer. Wrong population - does not meet selection criteria.

This study evaluates three chemotherapy regimens (MCA, MCAF, MLF) in patients with advanced uterine corpus carcinoma. While the design is not fully clear from the abstract, it appears to involve treatment comparisons in advanced disease and should be included for further review.
This is a methodological paper about meta-analysis techniques for time-to-event data, not a clinical trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.
This appears to be a review article about changes in endometrial cancer treatment, not a randomized controlled trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a systematic review about adjuvant (postoperative) chemotherapy for endometrial cancer. The selection criteria explicitly exclude trials of adjuvant treatment. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a systematic review about hormonal therapy (not cytotoxic chemotherapy) for advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer. The review objective focuses on cytotoxic chemotherapy, not hormonal therapy. Does not meet selection criteria.
This appears to be a review article about endometrial cancer treatment and lymphadenectomy, not a randomized controlled trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a retrospective observational study examining the clinical course of 520 patients with endometrial carcinoma, not a randomized controlled trial comparing chemotherapy interventions. Does not meet selection criteria.

This is a Phase III RCT comparing standard timed versus circadian timed doxorubicin+cisplatin chemotherapy in 342 patients with stage III, IV, or recurrent endometrial carcinoma. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions (different timing) in advanced disease.

This is a Phase III RCT comparing doxorubicin alone versus doxorubicin+cisplatin in 281 patients with stage III, IV, or recurrent endometrial carcinoma. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.

This is an RCT comparing doxorubicin alone versus doxorubicin+cisplatin in 177 patients with advanced and/or recurrent endometrial adenocarcinoma. Meets selection criteria as it compares chemotherapy interventions in advanced disease.
